datasetIdentity.flopCaveat: total_flos is the trainer's estimate of floating-point operations. It depends on token counts, sequence handling, and the accounting implementation of the library version in use. Equal totals establish a compatible total computational and token workload; unequal totals can arise from accounting differences between package versions as well as from different text. Neither proves nor disproves identity of the training text.

definitions.fourBitBaseComputeDtype: bnb_4bit_compute_dtype set by the trainer for the dequantised base-weight operations; it does not describe every training operation and says nothing about the LoRA optimizer or update precision
definitions.savedAdapterDtype: dtype in the safetensors header of adapter_model.safetensors
definitions.ggufStorageDtype: tensor dtype in the LoRA GGUF file
definitions.inferenceBaseQuantization: quantization of the Ollama base blob the adapter is applied over
definitions.optimizerUpdatePrecision: dtype of optimizer states and parameter updates during training; unverified for every run because no optimizer state was examined

notes: A BF16 adapter on disk shows the LoRA parameters were BF16 when PEFT saved them; it does not show the dtype of optimizer states or updates during training.

The VM trainer set float32 as the 4-bit base compute dtype and disabled autocast; the cpu-qlora-test experiment on the same venv with the plain Trainer saved F32, so the BF16 saves belong to the TRL 1.12 / transformers 5.16 path.

No GGUF was compared numerically with its source adapter. v1's F32-saved weights are stored as F16 (a narrowing, effect unmeasured); v3's BF16-saved weights are stored as F32 (a widening, exact only if the converter performed a plain cast; tensors not compared); v4-VM's BF16 adapter was converted to an F16 GGUF and the numerical effect of that conversion was not measured; v2 and v4-Tillicum store F32-saved weights as F32 (tensors not compared).

smokeRunClarification.finding: No complete CSS 360 training phase took under ten seconds. The only such training phase is the 2026-07-21 smoke run, Slurm job 182727: 3.57 s of training over three optimizer steps on four examples, model load 74.58 s, total 81.86 s. A smoke run is not a model. Complete Tillicum training phases were 31.35 s (v1), 30.65 s (v2), and 78.50 s (v4-Tillicum) inside allocations of 54, 53, and 104 s.
smokeRunClarification.otherSubTenSecondValues: model load 7.0 to 7.8 s on the GPU; evaluation 1.2 to 4.0 s

nineteenMinuteClarification.finding: No CSS 360 training job of that length exists. Three inference serving sessions (job name css360-ft-infer, cancelled by the operator) were of that length.

sharedValidationEvalLoss.comparabilityNote: The two v4 eval losses share the same validation records and the same intended response-only objective, but SFTConfig.completion_only_loss (VM, TRL 1.12) and DataCollatorForCompletionOnlyLM (Tillicum, TRL 0.13) have not been shown to produce identical label masks; a direct numerical comparison is qualified until label-mask parity is verified.

evalLossComparability: The two v4 eval losses share the same validation records and the same intended response-only objective, but SFTConfig.completion_only_loss (VM, TRL 1.12) and DataCollatorForCompletionOnlyLM (Tillicum, TRL 0.13) have not been shown to produce identical label masks; a direct numerical comparison is qualified until label-mask parity is verified. None of v1, v2, or v3 is comparable with v4, because v4 changed both the validation data and the loss definition. Comparisons among v1, v2, and v3 are limited by unverified dataset identity.

limitations: Deployed code that night carried the model-testing route (ce07ded, 2026-09-10T22:52:57-07:00) and predated the shared grounded path (1104ad5); RAG and Fine-Tuned + RAG used different prompt templates, Ollama endpoints, decoding, context windows, and output caps, so their difference measured two pipelines, not the adapter.
The route returned retrieved chunks but not the prompt, so prompt equality cannot be audited from the saved results.
The fine-tuned output cap was 160 tokens; the current path uses 256.
RAG timing is wall time including embedding and retrieval; fine-tuned timing is the service's generation time.
Training-coverage labels were judged against the July laptop export, whose checksums differ from the v2 dataset's.
One judge, one greedy pass, 22 questions; the v3 edge rests on 4 questions.
The RAG path has since changed, so the RAG row is not a baseline for a new run.
The deployed commit is inferred from commit times, not from a deployment log.

benchmarkPrerequisites.requirement: Tokenise the same validation records through SFTConfig.completion_only_loss on the VM stack and through DataCollatorForCompletionOnlyLM on the Tillicum stack and compare the label arrays.
benchmarkPrerequisites.why: Identical masks make the two v4 eval losses directly comparable; different masks make them two different quantities.
benchmarkPrerequisites.scope: Required before any statement about the two v4 adapters' training outcomes; the served-answer benchmark scores generated text and does not depend on it.
